usdRate.sourceName: RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement, Ratios and Rates: INR-US$ spot rate (FBIL reference rate)
usdRate.note: Week ended 23 October 2026 (87.71 a year earlier). 2025 average 87.16 (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF).

inflation_cpi.sourceName: MoSPI All-India CPI (base 2024), provisional, via DD News
inflation_cpi.note: September 2026 year-on-year, provisional (August final 4.83%). MoSPI PDF could not be opened (certificate error), so read via the public broadcaster's report.

inflation_projection.sourceName: RBI target 4% (2-6% band); MPC projection for 2026-27 5.2% (October 2026); 5-year CPI average about 5%
inflation_projection.note: CPI averaged about 5% over 2021-2025 and the RBI projects 5.2% for FY27, so we plan with 5% rather than the 4% target.

policy_rate.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India, Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 5-7 October 2026
policy_rate.note: Raised 25 bp to 5.50% (SDF 5.25%, MSF 5.75%); still 5.50% in the RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement for the week ended 23 October 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement, Ratios and Rates: savings deposit rate
savings_account_rate.note: Rate at major banks. Post Office savings accounts pay 4%.

fdr_3m_rate.note: RBI and the Ministry of Finance publish no 3-month deposit rate (Post Office time deposits start at 1 year); the only 3-month figures found were individual banks' card rates and broker pages, which we do not cite.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement, Ratios and Rates: term deposit rate over 1 year at major banks (6.00%-6.75%)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Midpoint of the RBI's 6.00%-6.75% range for major banks' term deposits of more than 1 year. The Post Office 1-year time deposit pays 6.9% (Oct-Dec 2026).

dps_rate.sourceName: Ministry of Finance small savings rates for Oct-Dec 2026: Post Office 5-year recurring deposit, via Business Today
dps_rate.note: Government-set rate for the 5-year Post Office recurring deposit; bank recurring deposits earn the bank's term-deposit rate for the tenure.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: RBI, Lending and Deposit Rates of Scheduled Commercial Banks, October 2026: weighted average domestic term deposit rate on outstanding deposits

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.sourceName: Ministry of Finance small savings rates for Oct-Dec 2026 (National Savings Certificate), via Business Today
sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: NSC, 5 years, compounded annually, paid at maturity. Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme pays 8.2%, PPF 7.1%.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India, 91-Day, 182-Day and 364-Day T-Bill Auction Result: Cut-off

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India, Government Stock auction results: cut-off yield of 6.53% GS 2031
tbond_5y_rate.note: About 5 years to maturity; auction cut-off yield.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement, Ratios and Rates: 10-year G-Sec par yield (FBIL)
tbond_10y_rate.note: Week ended 23 October 2026 (6.49% a year earlier). The 6.94% GS 2036 auction on 16 October 2026 cut off at 7.3955%.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, India: withholding taxes (interest paid to residents)
tax_bank_interest.note: 10% withheld when interest from one bank, co-operative or post office deposit exceeds Rs 50,000 a year (Rs 100,000 for senior citizens); page reviewed 11 May 2026. Interest is finally taxed at the individual's slab rate (0-30%).

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No flat or withholding rate: NSC interest is added to income and taxed at the individual's slab rate (0-30%), with no TDS; under the old regime yearly interest is deemed reinvested and counts for the 80C deduction.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Wikipedia, Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (cites DICGC)
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank, principal and interest together, in force since 4 February 2020 (older than 2025, but no change found; article edited September 2026). dicgc.org.in refused connections, so a secondary source is used.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap: the Supreme Court set aside a 30% consumer-forum cap in 2024 and the RBI leaves card rates to issuers. The typical rate (about 3-3.75% a month) was found only on issuer and card-comparison company pages, which we do not cite.

equity_return_low.sourceName: Nifty 50 TRI CAGR (index data, Aug 2026): 1-year -0.35%, 3-year 8.99%, 5-year 8.3%, 10-year 12.0%; RBI 10-year G-sec 7.52%
equity_return_low.note: Recent years were weak (5-year index return about 8.3%), so the low case is about the after-tax safe rate.

equity_return_base.sourceName: Nifty 50 TRI CAGR (index data, Aug 2026): 1-year -0.35%, 3-year 8.99%, 5-year 8.3%, 10-year 12.0%; RBI 10-year G-sec 7.52%; NSC 7.7%
equity_return_base.note: The index earned about 12% a year over 10 years but only 8.3% over 5, so we cap the base at the after-tax safe rate (about 6.8-6.9%) plus about 3 points.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Nifty 50 TRI CAGR (index data, Aug 2026): 1-year -0.35%, 3-year 8.99%, 5-year 8.3%, 10-year 12.0%; RBI 10-year G-sec 7.52%
equity_return_high.note: A repeat of the 10-year index record plus a little.

gold_return_low.sourceName: INR per USD 87.71 (Oct 2025) to 94.94 (Oct 2026), RBI WSS; World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF
gold_return_low.note: Gold can lose value in rupees for years after a strong run like 2016-2026.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Dollar gold long-run trend about 4-5% plus rupee depreciation about 3% a year (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF)
gold_return_base.note: Rupee gold rose far faster over 2016-2026 in an exceptional rally; long-run we expect dollar gold plus rupee depreciation.

gold_return_high.sourceName: INR per USD 87.71 (Oct 2025) to 94.94 (Oct 2026), RBI WSS; World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF
gold_return_high.note: A strong gold decade plus faster rupee depreciation (the rupee fell about 8% against the dollar in the year to October 2026).

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: RBI: major banks' term deposits over 1 year 6.00%-6.75%, less 10% tax
fixed_income_return_low.note: Bank deposits after 10% tax give about 5.4-6.1%; lower for people taxed at higher slabs.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Post Office 1-year TD 6.9%, NSC 7.7%, 364-day T-bill 6.69%, less tax
fixed_income_return_base.note: A mix of bank deposits, government bills and small savings after tax at about 10%.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme 8.2%, NSC 7.7%, less tax
fixed_income_return_high.note: Best government savings schemes after tax at about 10%.

life_claim_settlement_rate.sourceName: IRDAI Handbook on Indian Insurance Statistics 2024-25, individual death claims by number, via Insurance Business Asia
life_claim_settlement_rate.note: By amount 97.18%. IRDAI site not read directly.

insurance_term_premium_table.sourceName: StockCalc.in term-insurance premium estimates for Rs 1 crore cover, FY 2026-27 (independent calculator; sells no insurance)
insurance_term_premium_table.note: Rs 1 crore cover, 30-year term, non-smoker, yearly: Rs 6,325 (18-25), 7,820 (26-30), 10,350 (31-35), 14,950 (36-40), 22,425 (41-45), 32,775 (46-50), 48,300 (51-55), 71,300 (56-60); per 1,000 of cover divide by 10,000. Smokers pay about 1.7x. No quote is given above 60, so the 65 band's upper end is the 56-60 quote and real premiums at 61-65 are higher.

health_hospitalisation_cost.sourceName: NSS 80th round (2025) health survey, average out-of-pocket spend per hospitalisation in private hospitals, via Counterview
health_hospitalisation_cost.note: NSS 80th round (January-December 2025): average out-of-pocket spend per hospitalisation Rs 50,508 in private facilities and Rs 6,631 in public ones. A surgical stay in a private hospital usually costs more.

health_premium_table.note: Indicative premiums for Rs 10 lakh cover were found only on insurer and insurance-intermediary pages, which we do not cite; no regulator or independent premium guide by age was found.

oop_health_share.note: Latest published figure is for 2023 (older than 2025).

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: MoSPI CPI health 1.40% (Sep 2026, new base); headline CPI plan 5%
goal_inflation_health.note: The new-series health CPI is unusually low; hospital and insurance costs have long risen faster than headline prices, so we plan with 3 points above general inflation.

goal_inflation_education.note: Private school and college fees rise faster than the education CPI, so we plan with 2 points above general inflation.

life_expectancy.note: Men 70.7, women 73.9. India's own SRS 2020-24 life table gives 70.6 (pulled down by the 2020-21 pandemic years). Latest published figure is for 2024 (older than 2025).

life_table_remaining.sourceName: Registrar General of India, SRS Abridged Life Tables 2020-24 (published May 2026)
life_table_remaining.note: Expectation of life at the start of each age interval, India, 2020-24 (asOf is the mid-period date; published May 2026, the latest official table).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025: 10.8) and UN WPP 2024 medium variant via PopulationPyramid.net (2040: 16.3, 2065: 33.4)
support_ratio.note: Working-age people per person 65+ = 100 / old-age dependency ratio.

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Employees' Pension Scheme 1995 (EPFO): pension age 58, via Wikipedia (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation)
retirement_age_default.note: Same for men and women and for anyone born after 1975; needs 10 years of service, reduced pension possible from 50. epfo.gov.in returned 403, so a secondary source is used. Many private employers retire staff at 58-60.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Central government FR 56(a); Lok Sabha reply, via Gconnect
retirement_age_government.note: Central government employees retire at 60 (Lok Sabha reply, November 2019; older than 2025, no change found); some states and cadres differ (e.g. some teachers and doctors 62-65).

retirement_return_low.sourceName: RBI: major banks' term deposits over 1 year 6.00%-6.75%, less tax
retirement_return_low.note: Plain bank deposits after 10% tax, or higher slab tax.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Post Office 1-year TD 6.9% and 364-day T-bill 6.69%, less 10% tax
retirement_return_base.note: Equal to the after-tax 1-year government deposit and bill rate (6.9% and 6.69% less 10% tax: about 6.0-6.2%).

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme 8.2% less tax
retirement_return_high.note: Retirees who fill the SCSS limit earn about 7.4% after 10% tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: After-tax safe rate about 6%; Nifty 50 TRI 5-year CAGR 8.3% (Aug 2026)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: A balanced mix earning little more than safe deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Mix of equity base 10% and fixed income base 6%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Roughly half equity and half safe fixed income over a working life.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: A growth-tilted mix in a good decade.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: PIB backgrounder on the National Social Assistance Programme (IGNOAPS)
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: What a pensioner receives is the central share (Rs 200 a month at 60-79, Rs 500 at 80+) plus a state top-up of Rs 50 to Rs 5,700; PIB puts the average pension at around Rs 1,100 in many states. Only for people in below-poverty-line families.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Age 60+ in below-poverty-line families; central amount rises to Rs 500 at 80 (not 90).

gratuity_rule.sourceName: Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 rule, carried into the Code on Social Security 2020 (in force 21 November 2025), via Wikipedia
gratuity_rule.note: 15 days' wages per completed year of service (monthly wage / 26 x 15), after 5 years' continuous service (waived on death or disablement; fixed-term employees qualify pro rata under the Code); capped at a ceiling notified by the government.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Atal Pension Yojana (PFRDA) contribution chart, via Indian Pay Calculator
public_pension_scheme.note: Guaranteed fixed pension Rs 1,000-5,000 a month from 60, then to the spouse for life; the corpus (Rs 1.7-8.5 lakh) goes to the nominee after both die. Not open to income-tax payers since Oct 2022. Contributions deductible under the old regime; pension is taxable. Formal-sector workers are in EPF/EPS instead.

fdr_3m.note: Banks offer terms from 7 days; Post Office time deposits start at 1 year.

fdr_1y.note: Post Office Time Deposit (1-5 years) is the government equivalent.

dps.note: Banks and the Post Office (5-year RD, 6.7%).

sanchayapatra_5y.note: 5-year government certificate sold at post offices; also Kisan Vikas Patra, PPF and the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme.

tbill_91d.note: Individuals can bid through the RBI Retail Direct portal.

tbond_5y.note: Through RBI Retail Direct or a broker.

tbond_10y.note: Through RBI Retail Direct or a broker.

equity_fund.note: SEBI-regulated; Nifty 50 index funds are widely available.

gold.note: Physical gold is legal and widely bought; BIS hallmarking applies. New Sovereign Gold Bond issues have stopped.

insuranceRegulator.name: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

insuranceComplaints.name: Council for Insurance Ombudsmen
insuranceComplaints.note: Complain to the insurer first; IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal also takes complaints.

pensionScheme.name: Atal Pension Yojana (PFRDA)
pensionScheme.note: Formal-sector workers are covered by EPFO (https://www.epfindia.gov.in/); NPS is open to all.

publicHealthCover.name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
publicHealthCover.note: Rs 5 lakh a year per family for eligible poorer households and for everyone aged 70+.

depositInsurance.name: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)

statistics.name: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
